title: AniPal Archipelago
headline: A village where companions work and interact.
premise: An island village with working companions, job changes, resource storage, shared shops, weather events, and saved world state.
proof: Companion jobs, usable storage, shared shops, and a changing island environment.

play.title: Give companions work and manage the island
play.description: Companions produce resources and carry them to storage. Change a companion’s job, manage chest contents, sell fish and buy bait at shops that rotate on a schedule, and see weather change the island. Gameplay recordings are still to be added.

explode.title: How the village’s work and saved state connect
explode.description: A scheduler organizes companion work. Lifetime checks prevent old tasks from affecting a newly deployed companion. Resource records, relationships, and ordered offline events keep the different parts of the village connected.

layers.title: 01 / Run jobs and interactions
layers.detail: Coordinate companion work, movement, and relationships.

layers.title: 02 / Check task lifetimes
layers.detail: Stop outdated tasks after job changes, pickup, or redeployment.

layers.title: 03 / Track resource ownership
layers.detail: Record transfers between piles, carried resources, and chests.

layers.title: 04 / Calculate offline progress
layers.detail: Process ordered events and publish the resulting saved state.

cases.title: Scheduling jobs and stopping outdated tasks
cases.player: Changing a job or picking up a companion must stop its previous tasks.
cases.technical: SimulationManager centralizes managed NPC records in indexed priority buckets with staggered update cadences. Yielding jobs capture model and job generations; IsManagedJobAlive checks both before continuing. Bucket reassignment is queued until after iteration. Bounded social processing and an XZ spatial grid reduce the set of nearby candidates before exact filtering.
cases.tradeoff: This is cooperative scheduling, not parallel Actor workers. Generations and cadences are source-verified; supported population and timing improvements have not been benchmarked.

cases.title: Calculating progress between visits
cases.player: Offline work depends on available supplies, free storage, and whether companions can work.
cases.technical: Offline rules propose events over plain-table snapshots. The kernel selects by event time, rule priority, and UUID, then executes and wakes parked rules whose constraints changed. A transporter can free a full pile and wake a fisher. Persisted counters and residual state support repeatable behavior for fixed inputs. Publication saves a prepared generation, applies and verifies live state, then saves a final generation with rollback branches around live adapters.
cases.tradeoff: The local staged publication protocol does not establish a cross-server profile lease or arbitrary-failure durability. The source audit found a PosterHandler Script/Module mismatch in the leave checkpoint. That path must be verified or fixed before reconnect footage is treated as coherent checkpoint proof. Arbitrary login-partition invariance is not established.

cases.title: Tracking resources and relationships
cases.player: The game tracks who holds a resource while it moves from a pile to a companion to storage.
cases.technical: ResourceLedger represents piles, carries, and chests as authoritative containers. Visible objects project that state. TransporterJob rechecks destination state and distance before delivery, removes the accepted quantity, and resolves leftovers. Directional social records separately retain bounded relationship and conflict history; two companions need not feel the same way about each other.
cases.tradeoff: Deposit and carry removal involve separate calls, so this is not universal losslessness under adapter failures. A social cause → state change → later consequence capture is still needed before promoting emergent behavior as runtime evidence.

cases.title: Choosing weather, tide, and sky events
cases.player: Weather, tide, and sky events change the island over time.
cases.technical: GeneralEventManager has each server propose events for an epoch-aligned half-hour slot. A DataStore UpdateAsync transform accepts one proposal per slot and rejects slots that are already decided or out of date. Compatible tide, weather, and sky combinations are resolved inside the transform, while random choices are made before it, so a retried write does not re-roll. Each record carries a revision and each category an activation token: two consecutive events with the same name stay distinct, and an expiry timer only resets a category whose token still matches. Local application is serialized and keeps the highest pending revision; MessagingService announces changes, and polling covers missed messages.
cases.tradeoff: The coordination structure is source-verified, but convergence across several live servers has not been tested, so this does not claim every server always shows the same event. It is application-level coordination on DataStore atomic updates, not a consensus protocol. Not every modifier in the event tables has a gameplay consumer.

cases.title: Shop rotations that match on every server
cases.player: The fish market changes its featured fish every hour and the bait shop restocks every five minutes, and every server works out the same offers for each rotation.
cases.technical: GlobalRotationManager keys each rotation to its UTC time slot and generates it from a seeded hash of that key: a seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle picks the featured and runner-up fish, and weighted selection without replacement picks the bait stock and quantities. Any server therefore derives the same rotation on its own. A server that finds no record for a new slot writes one through a DataStore UpdateAsync that will not replace a newer record, then serves whatever record the store holds; MessagingService pushes the change and a periodic poll covers missed messages. BaitShopManager tracks purchases per player and per rotation, so buying never reduces anyone else’s stock. It checks inventory space before charging, re-checks the allowance after the Doubloon deduction, and refunds if a concurrent purchase or a full inventory stops the item.
cases.tradeoff: Read directly from an August 2026 source snapshot, which matches the September audit’s description; not yet exercised across live servers. Servers can briefly disagree at a rotation boundary because each reads its own clock. Prices use the in-game Doubloon currency; AniPal has no registered Robux products.
claims: Editorial evidence: AniPal shared shops, source read 2026-09-10

cases.title: Picking up and redeploying a clothed companion
cases.player: A held companion preview preserves its identity and clothing during pickup and redeployment.
cases.technical: Layered-clothing cage assemblies are mapped onto R6 companion rigs. The held Tool retains a structurally rich but behaviorally inert preview; redeployment restores the world assembly and behavior. This is a secondary integration case within the larger living simulation.
cases.tradeoff: One selected outfit, species, and age combination still needs runtime verification. This does not establish universal exact-transform restoration.

notes: Companion scheduling, resource storage, environmental event handling, and persistence are reviewed in the supplied source audit. Current gameplay captures are pending.

The leave checkpoint has an unresolved PosterHandler Script/Module mismatch in the audit. Offline-return footage is deferred. No crash durability, cross-server profile locking, numeric NPC capacity, or guaranteed data preservation is claimed.
The shared shop rotation was read directly from an August 2026 source snapshot, which matches the September audit’s description. It has not been exercised across live servers.

features.title: Companion jobs and job changes
features.description: Assign work around the island, then change a companion’s job while other companions keep working.

features.title: Inventories and storage chests

features.title: Shared shops
features.description: The fish market’s featured fish change every hour and the bait shop restocks every five minutes. Every server works out the same offers for each rotation, while each player keeps their own purchase allowance.
sources: Source read 2026-09-10 (August 14 autosave): GlobalRotationManager, BaitShopManager, TidalMarketManager
features.note: Prices use the in-game Doubloon currency. The rotation has not yet been checked across live servers.

features.title: Weather and environmental events
features.description: Weather, ocean, and sky events change the island’s appearance.
features.note: The planned clip shows one server. Synchronization between servers has not been demonstrated.

features.title: Saved world state
features.description: Profiles store companion identity, work state, resources, and placed storage.
features.note: The audit found a leave-checkpoint issue. AniPal’s save-and-return and offline-work demonstrations are deferred while that path is verified.
